overview: Close contract drift by implementing GET /documents/:id/render?page=N and making the viewer + RH1 proof use the returned render_url (signed, Range-capable).
goals: Implement the canonical render_url contract so 0001b viewer acceptance criteria are verifiable against the real API.
Ensure the render_url target supports Range requests so RH1 evidence is meaningful for the real pipeline.
nonGoals: Migrating fixture seed snapshots from filename-based document identifiers to DB document ids.
Production S3 presigning integration (PoC can use an app-signed URL; production can swap behind the contract later).
successMetrics: RH1 evidence is re-recorded for the actual render_url target and meets thresholds.
0001b viewer PRD US-001 AC-002 and US-002 AC-004 are unblocked by contract-aligned implementation.
openQuestions: For PoC, should render_url be a query-signed app route (presigned-style) or should pdf.js use header-signed requests (httpHeaders)?
Should /matters/viewer be replaced by /viewer/:documentId, or keep both and deprecate later?

stack.hosting: Local dev; default deployment target is a Hetzner VM (Vercel optional for previews)
stack.auth: PoC can run without auth in local/dev; production-minded deployments should enable auth

routes.name: Render URL
routes.purpose: GET /documents/:id/render?page=N returns { document_id, page, render_url } (page is 1-indexed).

routes.name: Document Viewer
routes.purpose: Fetch render_url server-first and render via pdf.js with page + zoom.

routes.name: RH1 PDF Perf Harness (Dev-Only)
routes.purpose: Run serial/spam page-jump tests and download results JSON; must prove Range on render_url target.

uiNotes: Viewer must use server-first fetch of render_url; no client-side fetch-by-default.
render_url target must be Range-capable (Accept-Ranges: bytes; Range returns 206).
Feature-flagged rollout: FEATURE_PDF_VIEWER gates /viewer/* entry points.

fields: render_url is a signed URL to the whole PDF (what pdf.js loads)
page is 1-indexed and used for initial viewer state/validation
supports Range and returns 206 Partial Content

importFormat.description: Verification uses fixture PDFs under docs/08-example-data/* and the existing upload flow (scripts/us002_smoke.ts) to create DB documents with storage_key.

rules: Signed URLs (render_url) are generated on demand with short TTL; never persisted; never included in traces/provenance; never logged.
render_url target must serve the whole PDF and support Range (pdf.js compatible).
The PDF bytes endpoint validates storage keys (allowlist) and prevents path traversal; no arbitrary filesystem reads.
All route boundaries use Zod validation and the standard safe error envelope (include trace_id).
Dev-only endpoints remain under /spikes/* and return 404 outside development.

stories.title: Fetch a signed render URL for a document
stories.description: As a reviewer/developer, I want to request a render_url for a document so that pdf.js can load it safely.
acceptanceCriteria: AC-001: GET /documents/:id/render?page=N returns { document_id, page, render_url } and validates document exists; page is 1-indexed and within [1..page_count] when page_count is known.
AC-002: render_url points to a URL that serves the whole PDF and supports Range: Accept-Ranges: bytes and Range: bytes=0-10 returns 206 Partial Content with Content-Range.
AC-003: Errors use the standard safe error envelope and include trace_id.
Example: Upload a PDF via the existing upload flow, then fetch render_url for page 1 and confirm the Range precheck passes against the returned render_url.
Negative case: Unknown document id returns NOT_FOUND (safe envelope).
Negative case: Page out of range returns VALIDATION_ERROR (safe envelope).

stories.title: Viewer and RH1 harness use the render_url target
stories.description: As a reviewer, I want the viewer and RH1 harness to use render_url so performance evidence matches the real pipeline.
acceptanceCriteria: AC-004: /viewer/:documentId?page=N fetches render_url server-first and loads the PDF in pdf.js using that URL.

AC-005: RH1 harness can be run against the render_url target and records Range proof + serial/spam perf JSON artifacts under docs/04-projects/02-features/0001_trust-substrate/spike-proofs/ and an updated summary/decision in spike-investigation.md.
Example: Run RH1 on pack_07_scans_rotated_low_quality via render_url and record evidence.
Negative case: If Range support is missing on the render_url target, the harness reports NO-GO and does not emit misleading perf numbers.

primaryObservableEffect: Viewer and RH1 proof run against the real render_url target (signed + Range-capable), eliminating contract drift from 0001b.
inScope: A signed PDF bytes endpoint used as the render_url target (Range + 206).
Viewer route /viewer/:documentId that fetches render_url server-first and renders via pdf.js.
RH1 proof updated to run against render_url target (not just /spikes/local-pdf).
functionalRequirements: FR-001: Signed URLs (render_url) are generated on demand with short TTL; never persisted; never included in traces/provenance; never logged.
FR-002: The PDF bytes endpoint validates storage keys (allowlist) and prevents path traversal; no arbitrary filesystem reads.
FR-003: The PDF bytes endpoint supports single-range requests and returns correct 206 responses (pdf.js compatible).
FR-004: Viewer remains client-only for pdf.js imports (dynamic import boundary); server components fetch render_url server-first.
FR-005: All route boundaries use Zod validation and the standard safe error envelope.
failureStatesUx: Render URL fetch fails: explicit error panel with safe code + retry/back.
Render URL expired/unauthorised: explicit error panel instructing retry (server will mint a new URL).
Range request invalid: return 416 and surface a viewer error state (no silent partial rendering).

metrics: RH1 totalMs p50/p95/max on render_url target

rollbackDisablePlan: Feature flag: FEATURE_PDF_VIEWER gates /viewer/* entry points.
Safe fallback: keep /spikes/local-pdf for local debugging, but treat it as non-authoritative for RH1 closure once render_url exists.

blockedBy: RH1 pdf.js performance on scanned/rotated PDFs (must be proven on render_url target)
dependencies: Documents have storage_key (object store) and ideally page_count for bounds validation.
risks: Signed URL leakage via logs/traces if not treated as secret.
Range implementation bugs can break pdf.js or invalidate RH1 measurements.
